title: Print Size of Fundamental Types
description: Write a program that uses the sizeof operator to display the byte size of the following C++ fundamental types in this exact order, each on its own line: int, float, double, char, bool, long long. Use std::cout to print the type name, a space, the size in bytes, and the word 'bytes'. Format: 'typename X bytes'.

test_cases.expected_output:
int 4 bytes
float 4 bytes
double 8 bytes
char 1 bytes
bool 1 bytes
long long 8 bytes

int 4 bytes
float 4 bytes
double 8 bytes
char 1 bytes
bool 1 bytes
long long 8 bytes

title: Type Casting and Precision Formatting
description: Write a program that reads two integers from std::cin. Compute their integer division result and their floating-point division result. Cast one operand to double before dividing to force floating-point arithmetic. Print three lines: the integer division result, the floating-point result formatted to exactly 2 decimal places using std::fixed and std::setprecision, and the type name of each result ('int' for the first, 'double' for the second).

title: Enum Types and Struct Memory Layout
description: Define an enum called Status with values: ACTIVE=1, INACTIVE=0, PENDING=2. Define a struct called Student with fields: int id, char grade, double gpa. Write a program that reads an integer student id, a character grade, and a double gpa from std::cin. Assign them to a Student struct, set the status to ACTIVE, and print the struct fields on separate lines: the id, the grade character, the gpa formatted to 2 decimal places, and the numeric value of the ACTIVE status.

title: Declare, Initialize, and Print Variables
description: Write a program that declares four variables: an int named 'age' initialized to 20, a double named 'height' initialized to 170.5, a char named 'initial' initialized to 'A', and a bool named 'isStudent' initialized to true (print as 1). Print each variable on its own line in this order: age, height, initial, isStudent. Use std::cout for output.

title: Variable Scope and Shadowing
description: Write a program that declares a global variable 'counter' initialized to 100. In main(), declare a local variable 'counter' initialized to 1. Print the local counter. Then enter a block scope { } and declare another 'counter' initialized to 50. Print the block-scoped counter. After the block, print the local counter again. Then print the global counter using the scope resolution operator (::counter). Output exactly four lines.

title: Const, Constexpr, and Static Variable Lifetimes
description: Write a program with a function called 'countCalls' that uses a static int variable to track how many times it has been called. Each call increments the counter and prints the current count. In main(), call countCalls() three times. Then declare a const int PI = 3 and a constexpr int MAX = 100. Print PI and MAX on separate lines after the function calls. Total output: 5 lines (3 from the function, 2 from main).

title: Classify Number as Positive, Negative, or Zero
description: Write a program that reads a single integer from std::cin. Use an if-else chain to classify the number. If the number is greater than 0, print 'Positive'. If less than 0, print 'Negative'. If equal to 0, print 'Zero'. Output exactly one word on a single line.

title: Grade Calculator with Nested If-Else
description: Write a program that reads an integer score from std::cin (0-100). Use nested if-else statements to determine the letter grade: A for 90-100, B for 80-89, C for 70-79, D for 60-69, F for 0-59. Print the letter grade on a single line. Assume input is always a valid integer between 0 and 100.

title: Day of Week Using Switch Statement
description: Write a program that reads an integer from std::cin representing a day number (1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, 4=Thursday, 5=Friday, 6=Saturday, 7=Sunday). Use a switch statement to print the full day name on a single line. If the number is outside 1-7, print 'Invalid'. The switch must handle each case explicitly.

title: Sum of Numbers from 1 to N
description: Write a program that reads a positive integer N from std::cin. Use a for-loop to compute the sum of all integers from 1 to N (inclusive). Print the sum on a single line. For example, if N=5, output is 15 (1+2+3+4+5).

title: Factorial Using While Loop
description: Write a program that reads a non-negative integer N from std::cin. Compute N! (factorial) using a while-loop. The factorial of 0 is 1. Print the result on a single line. For example, 5! = 120.

title: Multiplication Table with Nested Loops
description:
Write a program that reads an integer N from std::cin. Print the multiplication table from 1 to N using nested loops. Each row i (1 to N) contains i*1, i*2, ..., i*N separated by single spaces. Each row ends with a newline. For N=3, the output is:
1 2 3
2 4 6
3 6 9

title: Add Two Numbers Using a Function
description: Write a program with a function called 'add' that takes two int parameters and returns their sum as an int. In main(), read two integers from std::cin, call the add function, and print the result on a single line.

title: Swap Two Values Using Pass-by-Reference
description: Write a program with a function called 'swap' that takes two int parameters by reference and swaps their values. In main(), read two integers from std::cin. Print them in their original order. Call swap. Print them again in the swapped order. Use the format: 'Before: X Y' and 'After: X Y' on two separate lines.

title: Recursive Fibonacci Function
description: Write a program with a recursive function called 'fibonacci' that takes an int n and returns the nth Fibonacci number. fibonacci(0) returns 0, fibonacci(1) returns 1, fibonacci(n) returns fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2). In main(), read an integer N from std::cin. Print the first N Fibonacci numbers separated by spaces on a single line. For N=7, output: 0 1 1 2 3 5 8

title: Array Sum and Average
description: Write a program that reads an integer N from std::cin, then reads N integers into an array. Compute and print the sum of all elements on the first line, and the average (as an integer using integer division) on the second line.

title: Find Min, Max, and Linear Search
description: Write a program that reads an integer N from std::cin, then reads N integers into an array. Then read a search target integer. Find and print the minimum value, the maximum value, and the 0-based index of the first occurrence of the search target. If the target is not found, print -1 for the index. Print all three values on separate lines: min, max, index.

title: Matrix Addition with Two-Dimensional Arrays
description: Write a program that reads two integers R and C from std::cin (rows and columns). Then reads R*C integers for matrix A (row-major order), then R*C integers for matrix B. Compute matrix C = A + B (element-wise addition). Print matrix C with R rows and C columns, elements in each row separated by a space.

title: Basic Class with Constructor and Getters
description: Write a program that defines a class called 'Rectangle' with private members 'width' and 'height' (both int). Provide a constructor that takes two parameters to initialize them. Provide public getter methods getWidth() and getHeight(). Provide a method getArea() that returns width * height. In main(), read two integers for width and height, create a Rectangle object, and print the width, height, and area on separate lines.

title: Student Records with Multiple Objects
description: Write a program that defines a class called 'Student' with private members: name (string), id (int), and gpa (double). Provide a constructor and public getters. Provide a method getGrade() that returns 'A' if gpa >= 3.5, 'B' if gpa >= 2.5, 'C' if gpa >= 1.5, otherwise 'F'. In main(), read an integer N (number of students), then for each student read their name (no spaces), id, and gpa. Create a Student object for each and print 'name id grade' on each line.

test_cases.expected_output:
X 1 A
Y 2 F
Z 3 B

title: Shape Inheritance with Virtual Area Method
description: Write a program that defines a base class 'Shape' with a virtual method area() that returns 0.0. Derive a class 'Circle' from Shape with a private member 'radius' (double). Derive a class 'Rectangle' from Shape with private members 'width' and 'height' (both double). Each derived class overrides area() using the const keyword. Use 3.14159 for PI. In main(), read 'C' followed by radius for a circle, or 'R' followed by width and height for a rectangle. Create the appropriate object and print the area formatted to 2 decimal places.
